name: evidence-3904
prompt:
Read-only adversarial audit. Do NOT edit files. Do NOT launch browsers. Do NOT run anything under scripts/runners/ (a benchmark is running right now and concurrent Chrome instances would corrupt its timing numbers). You MAY read files and run `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_human_model.py -q`.

Target: /Users/me/.hermes/skills/software-development/browser-interaction-qa

Context: this is a newly built Hermes skill for realistic browser interaction QA. It contains scripts/human_model.py (seeded typing model), scripts/app/ (instrumented local test page), scripts/runners/*.py|mjs (one per tool: playwright, playwright_jslane, cdp, puppeteer, selenium, selenium_bidi, rrweb, browser_use), t
reply:
I did not edit anything, launch a browser or run anything under `scripts/runners/`. `pytest tests/test_human_model.py -q` → **28 passed in 0.72s**.

**You need to know this first:** your benchmark is already contaminated. `ps` shows a codex builder (`codex --yolo exec … builder PLAYWRIGHT+PUPPETEER`) running `run_puppeteer.mjs --profile careful` with no `--text-file` at 12:13. At the same moment `bench_matrix.sh` was running `run_selenium.py --profile rushed`. Both write the same `bench/results/<runner>__<profile>__<mode>.json` names. `selenium_actions__rushed` (seed 11, 728 chars) and `playwright_jslane__rushed` (seed 7, 728 chars) did not come from the matrix, which uses seed 77 and the 295-char `bench_text.txt`. The tree is also changing while I read it: `final_run.sh` and `clean_matrix.sh` appeared mid-audit, and `run_cdp.py` grew by about 10 lines.

## 1. Defects (ranked)

1. **`run_playwright.py:166-168` and `run_puppeteer.mjs:162-165`** — any character outside the US layout (’ “ — é, emoji) goes to `keyboard.down(char)`. Both libraries then throw `Unknown key` (Playwright `coreBundle.js:22515`, Puppeteer `Input.js` assert), so the run fails on ordinary prose with curly quotes. The `SMALL_HOLD_MS` fallback at `run_playwright.py:156` can never run, because holds are clamped to at least 45 ms (`human_model.py:54`) and the cutoff is 35. Fix: if the char isn't in the layout, use `keyboard.insert_text` / `sendCharacter`.
2. **`run_selenium_bidi.py:197-201`** — it looks for `connection.input` on `driver.bidi_connection()`, which is the CDP-backed connection, so it gets an AttributeError and records "BiDi unsupported". But Selenium 4.52 has real BiDi input at `driver.input.perform_actions` (`selenium/webdriver/remote/webdriver.py:1592`, `bidi/input.py:229`). The "unsupported" verdict is wrong. Lines 314-325 also record *any* exception as `unsupported`. Fix: set `options.enable_bidi = True`, call `driver.input.perform_actions`, and record other exceptions as `failed`.
3. **`run_cdp.py:253` and `run_selenium.py:132`** — `"status": "ok"` and exit 0 are hard-coded, even when the text doesn't match. Fix: `status = "ok" if summary["page"]["exact_match"] else "failed"`.
4. **`human_model.py:597-611`** — `form` mode adds a `Tab` after every `\n` but leaves the `\n` in `expected_text`. In a textarea, focus leaves the field and the rest of the text lands somewhere else. In an `<input>`, Enter submits the form. Every multi-line form run must fail; I confirmed the plan output: `'\n', Tab, 'F','i','t','y'…`. Fix: don't type the `\n` when emitting a Tab, or split the expected text per field.
5. **`human_model.py:241-243`** — `planned_duration_ms` adds every `hold_ms` one after another, but the runners overlap holds with the next delay. For rushed seed 77 the real schedule is 64.6 s of delays; the plan claims 102.9 s. As a result Puppeteer's accurate 66.5 s run is reported as −36 s off schedule, and Playwright's 104.8 s overrun is reported as +1.9 s. That flips which tool looks most faithful. Fix: duration = sum of delays + the final hold.
6. **`common.py:62-65`** — if anything at all is listening on 8811, the runner silently reuses it and returns a dummy `Popen(["true"])`. `run_puppeteer.mjs:103,313` hard-code 8811 and skip `common` entirely. When runners overlap, whichever one started the server kills it in its `finally` (`run_playwright.py:282`) while the other is still typing. Fix: one ephemeral port per run, and check a marker before reusing a server.
7. **`run_cdp.py:223` / `run_selenium.py:107`** — the temporary Chrome profile directory is deleted when the `with` block exits, but Chrome is only killed later in `finally` (`run_cdp.py:276`, `run_selenium.py:151`). If deleting the directory fails while Chrome is still writing, the `except` branch records a finished run as `failed`. I have not seen this happen; it is a race. Fix: quit Chrome inside the `with` block, or pass `ignore_cleanup_errors=True`.
8. **`scripts/postrun.sh:5`** — `cd "$(dirname "$0")"` lands in `scripts/`, so `bench/matrix.log` and `.venv/bin/python` don't exist from there. It polls for 60 minutes, then every step fails. It is running now (pid 31921). Fix: `cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."`.
9. **`run_browser_use.py:36`** — hard-coded `/Users/me/.browser-use-env/bin/python3`. Lines 82 and 389 also mark a 32-character `Element.fill` as `ok`. Fix: read the path from an env var, and record `unsupported` for the typing-fidelity row.
10. **`run_rrweb.py:83-84`** — runs `npm i rrweb@2` on every run: needs network, the version floats, and it breaks offline. That contradicts SKILL.md ("Nothing is downloaded per run"). Fix: pin rrweb in `package.json` and only check it's installed.

## 2. Stability for repeated Hermes use

- **Fresh clone:** there is no `requirements.txt` or `pyproject`. The `.venv` lives inside the skill and was built from `~/.browser-use-env` (`pyvenv.cfg`); venvs hold absolute paths, so moving or copying it breaks it. `.pytest_cache`, `node_modules` and bench artifacts sit in the tree.
- **Second machine:** Chrome's path is hard-coded for macOS (`common.py:31`, `run_puppeteer.mjs:11`). `bench_matrix.sh:22` needs GNU `timeout` (Homebrew coreutils here). `webdriver.Chrome()` lets Selenium Manager download chromedriver at run time.
- **Missing Chrome looks like a pass:** `run_playwright.py:263` records a launch failure as `unsupported` and exits 0.
- **Import fragility:** `run_cdp.py` and `run_selenium.py` use `import common`, which only works when run as a script; `python -m scripts.runners.run_cdp` raises ModuleNotFoundError. `TEXT_SAMPLE` is duplicated in `run_puppeteer.mjs:12` and will drift.
- **No runner code is tested.** No test imports any `run_*.py`. Key mapping, Shift handling, hold/rollover timing and status logic have no coverage.
- **Tests that look like tests but aren't:**
  - `test_integration.py:96-118` drives its own `page.keyboard.press` loop, caps delays at 40 ms and ignores `hold_ms`. It tests the model, not any runner.
  - `test_integration.py:121-129` asserts on whatever JSON the last run left in `bench/results`. It skips on a fresh clone, and would **fail** today because `playwright_jslane__careful` has `exact_match: false`, levenshtein 4.
  - `test_human_model.py:46-48` is circular: `human_model.py:618-624` rescales delays to the target WPM, and the test then checks the WPM matches the target.
  - `test_human_model.py:51` hold-range check includes pause steps, whose hold is hard-coded to 45.
  - `human_model.py` (`forced_error_index`) forces at least one typo into every text, so `backspaces > 0` always passes. A 3-character form field gets a 100% typo rate.

## 3. Honesty

- **JS lane `exact_match` is manufactured** (`run_playwright_jslane.py:24-52`). It overrides the `value` property on `#txt-react` so the getter returns a hidden `__qaLogicalValue` that still contains the newlines, while the real input has them stripped. `__snapshot` reads `el.value` (`index.html:137,211`), so `final_text` comes from the patched getter, not from what the field holds. The rushed run's "ok, 728 chars, exact" into a single-line input is the result of that patch. `bench_matrix.sh:38` also deliberately pairs multi-line text with a single-line input.
- **The capability table is built by grepping source** (`bench_report.py:306-333`):
  - `selenium_bidi` gets "real keystrokes? YES" because the word `keydownaction` appears, though it typed nothing.
  - `playwright_jslane` gets "real keystrokes? YES" from 2 synthetic keydowns plus trusted `input` events. `execCommand` produces trusted input events, so `isTrusted_true` = 296 / 739 there.
  - `browser_use` gets "per-char delay? YES" because the word "delay" appears in its notes.
  - "rollover?" is YES whenever "held" or "pending" appears.
- **Runs compared on different texts and seeds:**
  - careful/compose texts were 32 (browser_use), 79 (puppeteer), 220 (rrweb), 295 (cdp/selenium/jslane/bidi) and 728 (playwright) characters.
  - rushed seeds were 77/77/77/11/7.
  - `drop_incomparable` (`bench_report.py:516`) compares only character count. Same-length different text and mixed seeds pass through.
  - `aggregates.json` omits selenium_actions, rrweb and browser_use, though their JSONs exist.
- **`planned_wpm` leaves out pauses:** careful shows 50.49, but the real schedule is 295 chars in 94.1 s, about 37.6 WPM.
- **SKILL.md and CONTRACTS.md claims that don't hold:**
  - `SKILL.md:68` and `CONTRACTS.md:124` point to `COMPARISON.md`, which is never written; the report goes to `references/tool-comparison.md`.
  - `SKILL.md:158` says the JS lane is "everything else identical", but the careful JS-lane run failed (levenshtein 4).
  - `SKILL.md:174` says Selenium's jitter is "the largest of the set". Jitter was never measured: Selenium careful was +42.8 s, CDP careful +39.5 s.
  - The same line says Playwright's shifted names are "the only reliable way to type capitals". CDP typed every capital without Shift and matched exactly.
- **browser_use** is recorded as `status: ok` while its own notes say it "did not execute the human plan".

## 4. Best tool, from the JSONs

The only clean comparison is **rushed/compose, seed 77, 295 chars**: cdp, playwright and puppeteer, all exact matches. The real schedule is 64.6 s of delays, about 203 ms per keydown; I computed that from the plan.

| Runner | Wall | IKI mean | Off real schedule |
|---|---|---|---|
| puppeteer | 66.5 s | 201.8 ms | about +3% |
| playwright | 104.8 s | 319.1 ms | +62% |
| cdp | 145.4 s | 453.3 ms | +125% |

Careful/compose has only one comparable pair (cdp and selenium, 295 chars): cdp 170.2 s, IKI 566; selenium 173.5 s, IKI 577, against a 94.1 s schedule. Both are about 80% slow.

- **(a) Typing fidelity: Puppeteer.** It hit the schedule within about 3% on the one clean run. That is one run, made while other Chrome processes were live, and it crashes on non-ASCII text (defect 1).
- **(b) Broad UI QA, least risk: Playwright.** 2 of 2 runs ok with exact matches (careful 728 chars, rushed 295, levenshtein 0), plus screenshot and trace zip. Mouse, scroll and navigation were never benchmarked; the report marks navigation+mouse UNTESTED for every runner. So this pick rests on ergonomics, not measurement.
- **(c) Replaying a consented real session: rrweb, with large caveats.** It is the only recorder/replayer. One run: 220 chars, "replay matches source final text: True", 1360 events, **0 mouse/wheel events**, replayed in 8.34 s at speed 8. What it recorded was a synthetic Playwright session, not a real one, and replay rebuilds the DOM in an iframe; it cannot re-drive a live app. Real-session replay is untested.

## 5. Verdict

Not stable enough to ship. The keystroke model is fine. The parts that produce the conclusions are not:
- Two runners report `ok` no matter what landed in the field.
- The JS lane patches the element it measures.
- The BiDi "unsupported" finding comes from probing the wrong object.
- The capability table is regex over source code.
- Planned duration counts holds back to back, which inverts the timing ranking.
- The Playwright and Puppeteer runners crash on curly quotes.
- Form mode cannot pass on multi-line text.
- The results directory is being written by at least two processes at once right now.
- Two machine-specific absolute paths remain (Chrome at `/Applications/…`, `~/.browser-use-env`), there is no dependency manifest, and the only end-to-end test checks a leftover file.

Before shipping it needs defects 1–5 fixed, results isolated per run, and a clean matrix run on one text and one seed with no other agents touching the directory.

name: evidence-1073
reply:
The typer is fixed and tested without any GUI. Nothing was typed on your screen.

**Root cause** (`human-type` lines 351-364, same code in `human_type.py`):
- When the typer went back to retype a few words, it deleted the wrong number of characters. It counted the words without the spaces after them, so it dropped or doubled characters. That's how "INSTRUTIONS" happened.
- Even when there was nothing to retype, it could still delete one character and type nothing back.

**Fix**
- It now deletes and retypes exactly the same text.
- New check before any key is sent: it plays the whole planned key sequence into an empty buffer and confirms the result matches the target text. If it doesn't, the typer tries a new plan up to 6 times, then types without typos, and otherwise stops without typing.

**Proof:** `htype_plan_test.py` runs 5 setups × 2000 random seeds, including paths, `+`, uppercase and newlines. It passes on uniclaw and on pro, and the old code fails it. Backups are saved as `.bak-20261119`. The new file was swapped in all at once, so the lane's typing wasn't interrupted.

**Still open**
- `human-type` is 612 lines, over our 500-line limit. Splitting it is a small separate job for later.
- The check can't catch a key the system drops while typing, so reading the text back after typing remains the final check.

The E43 lane driver is still running. I'll tell you when its first follow-up goes out.
